newsitem.title: IRAN: Aggression on Iran risks Gulf security - Khamenei.
newsitem.headline: Aggression on Iran risks Gulf security - Khamenei.

text.p: Iran's spiritual leader on Saturday said any aggression against the Islamic Republic could destabilise the whole oil-rich Gulf region.

"Any aggression or attempts to make Islamic Iran insecure will make the Persian Gulf more insecure for the enemies of the Iranian nation, particularly those living in glasshouses," Ayatollah Ali Khamenei said in a speech carried by the state-run news agency IRNA.
Khamenei, who is also the commander-in-chief of the Iranian armed forces, said Iran was not a threat to the region and that it was protecting Gulf security.

"Outside powers and their followers in the region should know that the security of the Islamic Republic of Iran cannot be separated from that of the region," he said in an address to a crowd of Iran's Revolutionary Guards.
"The day when Iran enjoys security and calm, the region will be calm too," he said.
Western powers and their Gulf Arab allies have in recent months repeatedly expressed cocern over Iran's rearmament programme, saying it was a threat to the region.

Leaders of five Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states called on Iran at the end of a three-day summit in Doha earlier this week to end its "occupation" of three Gulf islands claimed by council member the United Arab Emirates (UAE), and criticised Tehran's military development programmes and its deployment of surface-to-surface missiles in the region.
The GCC groups Saudi Arabia, Kuwaut, Qatar, United Arab Emirates, Oman and Bahrain. Bahrain did not attend the council's annual summit.
The United States has 27 warships in and around the Gulf as part of a "dual containment" policy to deter Iran and Kuwait's former occupier Iraq.
Iran, the region's non-Arab power, is strategically placed at the entrance to the Gulf, the narrow strait of Hormuz, through which 15 million barrels of oil pass a day.
